title: Onboard Eval: Quick Triage (13 Mar 2026)
body:
Purpose:
Quick triage snapshot covering the latest onboarding eval run for model v2.3.2 -> v2.4-beta (candidate). This is a working doc: capture high-signal failures, immediate mitigations, owner-action items, and a short experiment plan to validate hypotheses.

Context / recent changes (last 7 days):
- Candidate model: v2.4-beta (intended to be lower latency via kernel reshuffle + new kv-cache packing).
- Serving config change: default batch target reduced from 64->48 on dedicated dev pool (JIRA-ALG-1287).
- Prompt normalization: applied whitespace/emoji strip step to onboarding prompt pipeline.
- New promptset: onboarding_promptset_v3 (adds 150 examples aimed at structured output).

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Overall QA pass rate dropped from 92.1% -> 86.4% on onboarding_promptset_v3 after switching to v2.4-beta.
- Hallucination metric (precision of factual spans) increased: 3.2% -> 8.9% failure rate (notable).
- Structured-output formatting failures up 4x (mainly missing JSON keys or wrong key names).
- Latency improved median ≈ 8% but 95p tail unchanged.
- Immediate priority: stop auto-rollout to dedicated staging; re-enable canary to hosted dev for further evaluation.

Key signals (snapshots):
- promptset: onboarding_promptset_v3 (n=1,200 examples)
- pass_rate_overall: "86.4%"
- hallucination_rate_factual_spans: "8.9%"
- structured_output_fail_rate: "12.6%"
- median_latency_ms: "142"
- p95_latency_ms: "410"
- token-efficiency (tokens/output): "1.03x baseline"
- regression_diff_from-v2.3.2: "-5.7pp overall pass"

Top failure modes (ranked by volume and product impact):
1) Missing required JSON keys in structured responses (45% of failures)
   - Example prompt: "Extract fields: name, dob, id_number -> JSON"
   - Candidate response: "{\"name\": \"Alice\", \"id\": \"X123\"}" (missing dob; key renamed id->id_number)
   - Notes: Looks like tokenization / labeling of keys affected by whitespace-stripping normalization and subtle model changes in copy/replicate tokens.

2) Hallucinated factual spans in short-answer evals (25% of failures)
   - Example prompt: "When was the treaty signed?"
   - Candidate response: "The treaty was signed in 1912 at Geneva." (ground truth: 1908, location: The Hague)
   - Notes: Not pure prompt mis-spec; likely calibration/regression in knowledge-head after kernel reorder.

3) Truncated or abruptly ended completions (15% of failures)
   - Pattern: correct content but cutoff mid-sentence; often when expected tokens > 120.
   - Hypothesis: new kv-cache packing slightly reduces effective context capacity for longer-output prompts.

4) Formatting drift for list/bullet outputs (10% of failures)
   - Example: expected hyphenated bullets, got inline comma list.

5) Rare safety false-positives blocking allowed benign content (5% of failures)
   - Example: non-violent metaphor flagged; impacted 6 enterprise onboarding cases.

Promptset observations (onboarding_promptset_v3):
- Added 150 structured-output cases; these disproportionately show failure concentration (structured_output_fail_rate 21% on the new subset vs 9% on legacy subset).
- Several examples use non-ASCII whitespace (em-dash, NBSP) — normalization step strips them, possibly changing token boundary leading to key name mismatch.
- Coverage gap: no explicit tests for kv-cache-heavy sequences > 160 tokens; add 30+ test cases.

Preliminary hypotheses (ranked):
A) Tokenization & normalization mismatch: the whitespace/emoji strip preproc removed separators required for model to copy exact key names -> structured key renames/missing keys. (high plausibility for structured failures)
B) Kernel reorder + kv-cache packing reduced effective context for certain prompt archetypes -> truncation/regression on longer outputs. (medium plausibility for truncation)
C) Minor fine-tuning drift: soft re-weighting of factualheads in v2.4-beta causing factual hallucination increase. (medium plausibility)
D) Serving batch size change interacts with runtime scheduling causing rare safety classifier false positives (low plausibility but non-zero).

Immediate mitigations (actionable, short window):
- Action 1: Pause rollout of v2.4-beta to staging dedicated pool. Owner: Mateo Silva. Due: 2026-03-15. (JIRA-ALG-1289)
- Action 2: Re-run onboarding_promptset_v3 with preproc that DOES NOT strip non-ASCII whitespace (to test Hypothesis A). Owner: Priya Desai. Due: 2026-03-14. (quick A/B)
- Action 3: Route long-output onboarding cases to v2.3.2 canary until kv-cache packing is validated. Owner: Jordan Lee. Due: 2026-03-14.
- Action 4: Add 30 targeted long-context testcases to promptset and re-run. Owner: Anika Rao. Due: 2026-03-17.
- Action 5: Create temporary fallback mapping that tolerates alternate key names (id vs id_number) in validator to reduce immediate customer impact while we fix model. Owner: Applied-ML infra. Due: 2026-03-16. (engineering-ops)

Short experiments (to validate hypotheses):
- Exp A1 (normalize off): Compare structured output pass rate with and without whitespace strip on a 300-example stratified sample. Metric: structured_output_fail_rate. Timebox: 24h. Owner: Priya Desai.
- Exp B1 (kv packing ablation): Launch v2.4-beta without new kv-cache packing on dev pool, run promptset. Metric: truncation rate, median latency. Timebox: 48h. Owner: Jordan Lee.
- Exp C1 (factual calibration check): Run fact-precision sweep using held-out factual promptbank (n=500) across v2.3.2 and v2.4-beta; measure hallucination delta and logits distribution for factheads. Owner: Mateo Silva. Timebox: 72h.

Evidence to collect (priority):
- Full diff of tokenized prompt vs tokenized candidate for first 200 structured failures (download token streams).
- KV-cache occupancy traces for truncated cases (collect at serve-time).
- Safety classifier logs for the flagged safety false positives.
- Canary logs for batch scheduling when p95 spikes observed.

Risks & notes:
- Rolling back v2.4-beta entirely will regress latency improvements; need to isolate root cause before broad rollback.
- Some mitigation (validator key-tolerance) is merge-safe and should be prioritized to reduce customer facing breaks.
- If experiment A1 shows structured failures vanish w/ normalization off, we should revisit preproc and instead canonicalize keys via deterministic mapping rather than wholesale strip.

Next check-ins:
- Standup triage: 2026-03-14 10:00 PT (short 20m sync) — owners present with run results for Actions 2/3.
- Deep-dive: 2026-03-16 11:00 PT — present experiment outcomes and propose rollout plan.

Open questions (to resolve in syncs):
- Was whitespace/emoji strip first introduced with onboarding_promptset_v3 or previously? (trace required)
- Any correlated infra deploys at serving-scheduling layer between 2026-03-07 and 2026-03-12?
- Can validator mapping be released as a hotfix without breaking other downstream metrics?

Quick links / tickets:
- JIRA-ALG-1287 (serving config change)
- JIRA-ALG-1289 (pause rollout / staging hold)
- github PR: model-zoo/pulls/342 (v2.4-beta)

Notes to self: keep this doc minimal — move experimental logs and token dumps to linked confluence page and attach artifacts.

-- end of quick-triage snapshot --
